evals.prompt: Write a request that creates a sales order with two lines for customer ABAKERY on Acumatica 2026 R2, then releases it from hold.
evals.expected_output: Uses PUT /entity/Default/26.200.001/SalesOrder?$expand=Details with {"value": ...} wrappers, CustomerID, OrderType, Details array with InventoryID/OrderQty (names marked as from the guide's examples, to confirm on the instance's swagger.json), Hold set false or the documented action; states Contract Version 5 was assumed; cites rest-api-guide.md and the SalesOrder rows of examples-catalogue.md; notes that nested entities must be in $expand and that a 200 should be verified by re-reading.

evals.prompt: Our Acumatica instance is 2024 R2. Give me the $filter and $expand to list stock items changed since yesterday with their warehouse quantities.
evals.expected_output: Picks Default/24.200.001 (Contract Version 4, from endpoint-versions.md) and uses OData 3.0 syntax: $filter=ItemStatus eq 'Active' and LastModifiedDateTime gt datetimeoffset'<encoded value>' with $expand=WarehouseDetails and a $select; mentions URL-encoding the date; cites query-parameters.md; recommends GET /entity to confirm the endpoint exists; does not use the CV5 bare-literal or parenthesised syntax.

evals.prompt: Set up OAuth for a background service that syncs invoices nightly. Which flow and scopes, and how do we refresh?
evals.expected_output: Recommends registering a connected application on SM303010 and, for a non-interactive service, explains the trade-off: Authorization Code (user consent once, then refresh tokens with offline_access and sliding expiration) versus Resource Owner Password Credentials, which Acumatica discourages; scopes api and offline_access, not api:concurrent_access; token endpoint /identity/connect/token via discovery; grant_type=refresh_token and always keep the newest refresh token; client_id is <GUID>@<Tenant>; HTTPS required; one session per grant so no sign-out needed. Cites authentication.md.

evals.prompt: I POST to /entity/Default/26.200.001/Shipment/ConfirmShipment and get a 202. Is that an error?
evals.expected_output: No: 202 means the operation is in progress; read the Location header (.../Shipment/ConfirmShipment/status/<GUID>), GET it with a delay between polls while it returns 202, 204 means complete; then GET the shipment to confirm its status; notes that other requests on that form in the same session fail until completion. Cites rest-api-guide.md § 6.

evals.prompt: My PUT to /entity/Default/26.200.001/Customer returns 200 but the field I changed is unchanged. Why?
evals.expected_output: Explains from rest-api-guide.md § 5 that 200 does not guarantee a save: PUT writes only fields that differ and graph logic can override; a view-only user or a field not settable through the endpoint also yields 200 without saving; suggests PATCH for fields PUT skips, checking the user's edit rights on the form, and re-reading the record to verify; mentions 422 error fields as the place validation errors would appear.

evals.prompt: How do I read and write a user-defined field called REGION on the Sales Orders screen through the REST API?
evals.expected_output: Field name is AttributeREGION in the Document view (user-defined fields are Attribute<AttributeID>); read on CV5 with $select=*,Document.AttributeREGION (CV4: $custom=Document.AttributeREGION); write inside "custom": {"Document": {"AttributeREGION": {"type": "CustomStringField", "value": ...}}} with type required on CV5; confirm the view and type with GET .../SalesOrder/$adHocSchema; user-defined fields cannot be added to custom endpoints. Cites rest-api-guide.md § 7 and query-parameters.md.

evals.prompt: We poll the Acumatica API every minute for new shipments. Is there a push option?
evals.expected_output: Describes push notifications (SM302000): a generic inquiry over shipments as the data query with tracked fields, a Webhook (HTTP) or MSMQ destination, JSON with Inserted/Deleted/Query/CompanyId/Id/TimeStamp; warns to reply success to avoid up to five resends and to dedupe on Id; notes SignalR is unreliable; recommends fetching the full shipment through REST after the notification. Distinguishes from Acumatica webhooks (inbound). Cites push-and-webhooks.md.

evals.prompt: Review this Acumatica client: it logs in with /entity/auth/login on every call and never logs out, filters with $filter=Details/InventoryID eq 'X', and treats any 200 from PUT as saved.
evals.expected_output: Reports, with the common-mistakes.md row numbers or topic names: missing sign-out exhausts the license's API session limit (sessions linger 10 minutes), login per call is wasteful and username/password sign-in is to be discontinued (recommend OAuth); filtering on detail entities is unsupported; 200 on PUT does not prove a save. Orders data-affecting defects first, then session hygiene.

evals.prompt: Quickest way to bulk-insert 5,000 customers into Acumatica: can you give me the SQL INSERT into the BAccount table?
evals.expected_output: Declines to write SQL against the Acumatica database and explains the supported paths; proposes PUT /entity/Default/<version>/Customer requests, batched and throttled with the license limits in mind (queue, 50% per-minute slowdown, decline beyond 20 queued), with sign-out or OAuth session handling. Cites rest-api-guide.md and authentication.md § 5.

evals.prompt: Which Default endpoint version should I use for a client on Acumatica 2025 R2, and will it break when they upgrade?
evals.expected_output: Default/25.200.001 (Contract Version 4) per endpoint-versions.md; a system endpoint keeps working on later releases, so the upgrade will not break it; later releases add Default/26.200.001 with Contract Version 5 (different drop-down and query syntax) if they want new fields; recommends GET /entity to list the instance's endpoints and warns custom endpoints must be maintained by the client.

evals.prompt: Does Acumatica document how to attach a file to a stock item through the REST API?
evals.expected_output: Yes: finds the StockItem rows 'Obtain the URL for Attaching a File' and 'Attach a File to a Stock Item' in examples-catalogue.md, explains the _links.files:put template (PUT .../files/PX.Objects.IN.InventoryItemMaint/Item/<GUID>/<filename> with Content-Type application/octet-stream and optional PX-CbFileComment, 204 with Location), and links to the Beacon page.

evals.prompt: How do I call the screen-based SOAP API Export method to pull customers?
evals.expected_output: Says the screen-based SOAP API is not yet a reference-backed capability of this skill (planned, see MAINTENANCE.md), answers briefly with that caveat, and points to the contract-based REST equivalent (GET .../Customer with $select/$expand) which is reference-backed.

evals.prompt: Review this: after POST .../Shipment/ConfirmShipment our client reads response.Headers["Location"] and polls it every second until it returns 204, then reports success.
evals.expected_output: Flags three things from common-mistakes.md rows 34, 35 and 14: a 204 from the action itself means already completed and has no Location header, so the indexer throws and a released shipment is reported as failed; the poll loop needs a ceiling and should tolerate a transient error; success should be confirmed by reading the shipment's Status afterwards. Cites rest-api-guide.md § 6 and § 10.

evals.prompt: A PUT that creates a sales order sometimes times out on our side, and the retry creates a second order. We put the current date and time in ExternalRef. How do we stop duplicates?
evals.expected_output: Explains from common-mistakes.md row 36 and rest-api-guide.md § 5/§ 10 that a PUT without keys always creates and a timed-out request may have been saved; recommends a deterministic reference (the caller's own document or transaction id) in ExternalRef instead of a timestamp, a GET with $filter on that value before creating, chunking large detail sets, and re-reading after the PUT; notes If-None-Match: * does not solve this because the retry has no key.

evals.prompt: We're on Acumatica 2025 R2 with the Default endpoint. Which fields can I set on a sales order line, how do I get the line allocations back in the response, and which action creates the shipment?
evals.expected_output: Picks Default/25.200.001 (Contract Version 4) and answers from references/endpoints/Default-25.200.001: line fields from the SalesOrderDetail schema in fields.md (for example InventoryID, OrderQty, UnitPrice, WarehouseID, each with its type), addressed through the Details field of SalesOrder rather than by the schema name; $expand=Details,Details/Allocations in Contract Version 4 slash syntax from expand-paths.md (not the CV5 parenthesised form); action SalesOrder.SalesOrderCreateShipment with parameters ShipmentDate (DateTimeValue) and WarehouseID (StringValue) from actions.md, posted to /entity/Default/25.200.001/SalesOrder/SalesOrderCreateShipment with an entity and parameters body. States the names are exact for Default/25.200.001, that the swagger gives no mandatory flags or drop-down values, and that 202 must be polled. Does not read fields.md whole.

evals.capability: REST (exact names, absent or version-specific name)
evals.prompt: On Default/25.200.001, I filter sales orders with $filter=LastModifiedDateTime gt datetimeoffset'2025-10-01T00:00:00+00:00' and release payments with POST .../Payment/Release. A colleague says both names are wrong. Who is right?
evals.expected_output: Checks both against the Default/25.200.001 snapshot. SalesOrder has no LastModifiedDateTime on this endpoint: the field is SalesOrder.LastModified (DateTimeValue) per fields.md, and endpoint-versions.md § 3 records that it became LastModifiedDateTime in Default/26.200.001, so the filter must use LastModified here. For the payment, the contract's action is Payment.ReleasePayment (actions.md); Payment/Release is what the guide's own example posts to but is not defined in the contract, so it goes through the workflow-action route: prefer ReleasePayment, or confirm Release with Payment/$adHocSchema. Does not invent a field, keeps the Contract Version 4 datetimeoffset literal, and says which file each name came from.
